$comment: BC Transit's Fraser Valley systems in one export, published by BC Transit through Consat (tmix.se) as operator 13 (https://www.bctransit.com/open-data/, checked 2026-11-01): Central Fraser Valley (Abbotsford and Mission), Chilliwack, Agassiz-Harrison, Hope and the 66 Fraser Valley Express; one agency, every route_id ending in -CFV. Every route is drawn; overrides and exclusions: routes.json. Regions showing it: fraser-valley. Terms: https://www.bctransit.com/open-data/terms-of-use/ (identify BC Transit as the source; no use of its marks).
name: BC Transit (Fraser Valley)
$timezoneChecks: Known facts about the feed's time zone that the runtime's time zone data (tzdata, via ICU) must agree with; the server refuses to start otherwise (checkTimezoneData in packages/transit-core/src/time.ts). Times are still always computed from the runtime's data, never from these. BC moved to permanent UTC-7 in 2026 (tzdata 2026b, https://data.iana.org/time-zones/tzdb/NEWS); older data falls back to UTC-8 on 2026-11-01.

timezoneChecks.reason: British Columbia's permanent UTC-7 (tzdata 2026b or later)

static.$comment: Regenerated daily with a new feed_version (e.g. "202611010/20261031 21:00:00/20261101 04:00:00") even when the timetable is unchanged, so fetch-gtfs archives a version only when its files differ from the newest archived one. No dated history. Uses calendar_dates.txt only (no calendar.txt), shape_dist_traveled in metres. How often the timetable really changes: config/regions/fraser-valley/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #1.

realtime.$comment: No API key and no stated request limit. Every bus in the four systems, with its trip; 25 buses at 10:00 on Sunday 2026-11-01, fixes 1-26 s old when fetched. Polled within a modest budget all the same: config/regions/fraser-valley/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #2.
realtime.$poll: Positions and trip updates every 2 minutes while buses run (05:00-24:00), every 5 overnight; alerts every 5 minutes, 15 overnight. Every 2 minutes is the default for BC Transit systems other than Victoria and Kelowna (Braden MacDonald, 2026-11-01; config/operators/bc-transit/operator.json): smaller systems, less often. About 1,510 requests a day; dailyCap is a safety net. OPEN-QUESTIONS #2.
realtime.$staleGraceS: Clients fall back to schedule estimates once live data is this much older than the positions poll interval: one missed 2-minute poll (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$coverageSlackS: Recorder coverage breaks when snapshots are further apart than the positions poll interval plus this (guess, near TransLink's 55 s at similar intervals; OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$interpolateSlackS: Interpolate between two fixes at most the positions poll interval plus this apart: across one missed 2-minute poll (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$extrapolateSlackS: Predict a bus forward for at most the positions poll interval plus this (fixes are fresher than TransLink's: under 30 s old when fetched; guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).

display.$tripId: Trip ids are three internal ids, <journey>:<variant>:<block> (e.g. 2571443:14945993:14954744); the journey alone is unique on any date (feed of 2026-11-01: each of its 2,320 trips has its own journey).
display.$feedVersion: Versions look like "202611010/20261031 21:00:00/20261101 04:00:00": the export date and a sequence number, then the export window.
